title: Heartbeat
subtitle: 「心跳／脈搏／心律」，究竟是哪一種 heartbeat？
description: 「心跳／脈搏／心律」，究竟是哪一種 heartbeat？

words.note: 日常與醫療中都很常見。它通常不是「心臟本身的一跳」，而是心臟收縮後在動脈中形成、可摸到的脈動。
words.example: The nurse checked his pulse at the wrist.
words.exampleZh: 護士在他的手腕量脈搏。

exercises.original: The nurse checked his heartbeat by placing two fingers on his wrist.
exercises.zh: 護士把兩隻手指放在他的手腕上檢查脈搏。

options.explanation: two fingers on his wrist 是決定性線索。手腕上摸到的是動脈的 pulse，而不是直接摸到心臟本身的一次 heartbeat。
heart rate 是每分鐘次數；雖然可由脈搏估算，但這句描述的是觸診動作本身。
指一次完整的收縮—舒張生理週期，不會在手腕以這種方式直接「check」。
可由 pulse 感受節律是否規則，但原句首先指摸到的脈搏。
通常需要血壓計，而不是只用兩指觸診。
是形容詞「有脈動的」，不能作名詞賓語。

exercises.original: She could feel her heartbeat clearly in her neck after running.
exercises.zh: 跑步後，她能清楚感到頸部的脈搏。

options.explanation: 頸部可感到的是動脈搏動，尤其運動後更明顯；這是典型 feel one's pulse。

options.text: cardiac beat inside the heart only
options.explanation: 語義過窄且位置不符；她感覺的是頸動脈搏動。
血壓不是能直接感覺成一下下搏動的名稱。
是生理週期概念。
需要聽而不是在頸部「feel」。
詞性不合。

exercises.original: The doctor felt the patient's heartbeat at the radial artery.
exercises.zh: 醫生在橈動脈觸摸病人的脈搏。

options.explanation: radial artery 是標準量脈搏位置，因此名詞應是 pulse。
心音是用聽診器在胸前聽。
醫生可由 pulse 計算 rate，但「felt at the radial artery」直接指 pulse。
需要另外測量。
rhythm 是模式，不是動脈本身摸到的波動名稱。
pulsation 是名詞，不是 adjective；而這裡固定搭配仍是 pulse。

words.note: 非常接近一次 heartbeat 的自然簡稱，可指心臟的一次跳動，也可指一連串節拍中的一下。
words.example: The monitor recorded every beat of her heart.
words.exampleZh: 監察器記錄了她每一下心跳。

exercises.original: The monitor recorded every heartbeat during the test.
exercises.zh: 監察器在檢查期間記錄每一下心跳。

options.explanation: every 要求可數的一次次事件，every beat 正好表示每一下心臟跳動。
rhythm 是連續跳動的模式，不是每一個可數事件。
rate 是頻率數值，例如 70 bpm。
不同生理指標。
仍是每分鐘次數，不是每一下。
通常不可數地描述持續動作；every beating 不自然。

exercises.original: He heard each heartbeat clearly through the headphones.
exercises.zh: 他透過耳機清楚聽到每一下心跳。

options.explanation: each + audible individual event strongly supports beat.
would refer to the pattern formed by many beats, not each sound event.
a number, not what is heard as each individual sound.
also a number.
not audible as discrete beats in this sense.
past participle of beat, not the noun.

exercises.original: Between two heartbeats, the monitor briefly showed a flat line.
exercises.zh: 兩次心跳之間，監察器短暫顯示平線。

options.explanation: between two requires two discrete heartbeat events.
a person normally has one ongoing rhythm rather than one rhythm between another rhythm in this sentence.
rate is a measurement across time, not a momentary beat.
different measurement.
a frequency, not individual events.
continuous process, not naturally counted as two beating.

words.note: 強調心跳是否規律、快慢是否有模式，而不是單獨一次跳動。
words.example: The doctor listened carefully to the rhythm of his heart.
words.exampleZh: 醫生仔細聆聽他的心臟節律。

exercises.original: The doctor listened to the heartbeat to see whether it was regular or irregular.
exercises.zh: 醫生聽心跳，判斷節律是否規則。

options.explanation: regular or irregular 是節律判斷的直接線索；rhythm 描述多次心跳之間的時間模式。
單一 beat 本身不能稱為「regular or irregular」的完整模式。
rate 判斷快慢，不直接等於 regularity。
也是頻率。
不同指標。
形容詞，句中需要名詞。

exercises.original: The device checks the heartbeat pattern for unexpected irregularities.
exercises.zh: 裝置檢查心跳節律是否有意外不規則情況。

options.explanation: pattern + irregularities clearly points to temporal rhythm rather than number of beats.
one beat is too narrow.
not timing pattern.
rate may be normal even when rhythm is irregular.
sound quality is not the same as rhythm.
adverb.

exercises.original: Her heartbeat settled into a regular pattern after she rested.
exercises.zh: 休息後，她的心跳恢復規律節奏。

options.explanation: 固定搭配 settle into a regular rhythm 正好描述心跳時間模式恢復規律。
rate 可以下降，但 regular rate 不等於 rhythm regularity。
是收縮壓與舒張壓的差值，完全不同。
只是次數。
範圍太廣，不能精確替代 rhythm。
rhythmicity 是名詞，不是 adjective；且一般語境用 rhythm 更自然。

words.note: 比單獨 rhythm 更明確，常見於一般醫療說明。
words.example: The test showed a normal heart rhythm.

exercises.original: The ECG showed that her heartbeat pattern was normal.
exercises.zh: 心電圖顯示她的心律正常。
exercises.upgrade: heart rhythm · 心律；心臟節律

options.explanation: ECG + normal pattern is a standard heart-rhythm context.
ECG can show rate, but pattern specifically points to rhythm.
measured peripherally and focuses on count per minute.
not what ECG measures.
refers to one physiological contraction-relaxation sequence, not overall regularity.
word class/order is wrong.

exercises.original: The medication can affect the heartbeat pattern in some patients.
exercises.zh: 這種藥物可能影響部分病人的心律。

options.explanation: medication + effect on timing pattern is a standard medical-neutral use.
rate is narrower and does not include irregular timing patterns.
different parameter.
sound quality is not the intended electrical/timing pattern.
one-cycle physiology is too narrow.
not the noun phrase required.

exercises.original: Exercise normally changes heartbeat speed without necessarily making the pattern abnormal.
exercises.zh: 運動通常會改變心跳速度，但不一定令心律異常。

options.explanation: the corrected sentence contrasts rate (speed) with rhythm (pattern). abnormal heart rhythm is the precise expression.
already fills the speed concept; using it again would erase the intended distinction between speed and pattern.
unrelated pressure measure.
volume of blood pumped per minute, not rhythm.
not pattern.
wrong word order.

words.note: 較正式、醫療化，是 heart rhythm 的專業版本。
words.example: The device continuously monitors cardiac rhythm.

exercises.original: The monitor continuously records the patient's heartbeat pattern in the intensive care unit.
exercises.zh: 監察器在深切治療部持續記錄病人的心律。
exercises.upgrade: cardiac rhythm · 心律；心臟節律

options.explanation: ICU + continuous monitoring calls for formal clinical terminology; cardiac rhythm precisely names the heart's timing pattern.
count gives rate, not irregularity pattern.
different vital sign.
different measurement.
one-cycle physiology, not continuous rhythm.
adjective phrase, not noun.

exercises.original: The report noted an abnormal heartbeat pattern during the night.
exercises.zh: 報告指出夜間出現異常心律。

options.explanation: abnormal + pattern + formal report is a textbook cardiac-rhythm context.
one beat cannot represent a sustained rhythm pattern.
focuses on frequency.
unrelated.
auditory quality, not electrical/timing pattern.
cardi- is not used this way as a free adjective; use cardiac.

exercises.original: The device is designed to detect changes in the heartbeat's timing pattern.
exercises.zh: 裝置旨在偵測心律時間模式的變化。

options.explanation: timing pattern directly defines rhythm in clinical language.
rate is only how many beats per minute.
different measure.
blood volume per minute.
strength of pulse, not timing pattern.
rhythmicity is a noun, but cardiac rhythm is the standard phrase here.

words.note: 較技術、醫療，表示心臟的一次搏動。
words.example: Each cardiac beat pushes blood into the circulation.
words.exampleZh: 每一次心臟搏動都把血液推進循環系統。

exercises.original: Each heartbeat pushes blood out of the heart.
exercises.zh: 每一次心臟搏動都把血液推出心臟。
exercises.upgrade: cardiac beat · 心臟搏動；一次心跳

options.explanation: each + physiological pumping action identifies one discrete heart contraction event.
rhythm is the pattern across many beats.
a count per minute.
peripheral count per minute.
pressure outcome, not the beat event.
not the required noun phrase.

exercises.original: The sensor detected every heartbeat during the procedure.
exercises.zh: 感應器在程序期間偵測到每一次心搏。

options.explanation: every again requires countable individual events.
not individually countable in this way.
measured across time, not each event.
different physiological variable.
too broad; it could include electrical activity beyond individual beats.
wrong word order.

exercises.original: The diagram shows what happens during a single heartbeat.
exercises.zh: 圖表顯示一次心臟搏動期間發生的情況。
exercises.upgrade: cardiac beat · 一次心臟搏動

options.explanation: single makes the individual beat sense explicit.
rhythm necessarily spans multiple beats.
a per-minute measure.
same.
not the event.
would refer to the general ongoing action, not one discrete beat.

words.note: 解釋性很強，表示心臟持續跳動這個動作或現象。
words.example: Exercise makes the beating of the heart more noticeable.
words.exampleZh: 運動會令心臟跳動感更明顯。

exercises.original: Exercise made his heartbeat much more noticeable in his chest.
exercises.zh: 運動令他胸口的心臟跳動感變得明顯得多。
exercises.upgrade: beating of the heart · 心臟跳動；心搏

options.explanation: the sentence describes the ongoing physical sensation of the heart beating, not a numeric rate or one isolated beat.
not usually directly felt as chest beating.
rate is numerical and narrower.
blood volume pumped per minute, not subjective beating sensation.
the sentence says noticeable in the chest, which can be felt rather than just heard.
wrong grammatical analysis.

exercises.original: In a quiet room, the heartbeat may seem unusually loud to a nervous person.
exercises.zh: 在安靜房間裡，緊張的人可能覺得自己的心臟跳動特別響。
exercises.upgrade: beating of the heart · 心臟跳動

options.explanation: seem unusually loud points to the ongoing audible/physical phenomenon of heart beating.
not audible.
number, not loudness.
not audible.
technical physiological sequence, not everyday perceived sound.
not grammatical.

exercises.original: The stethoscope makes the heartbeat easier to hear.
exercises.zh: 聽診器令心臟跳動更容易聽到。
exercises.upgrade: beating of the heart · 心臟跳動

options.explanation: the clue is audibility of the ongoing beating process.
can be calculated from sounds, but a rate itself is not “heard” as a noun object.
not what a stethoscope alone directly makes easier to hear in this sentence.
again numerical.
not audible.
not the required noun phrase.

words.note: 較自然、略帶描述或文學色彩，強調所感覺／聽到的心臟跳動。
words.example: In the silence, he could hear the heart's beating in his chest.
words.exampleZh: 寂靜中，他能聽到胸口的心臟跳動。

exercises.original: In the silence, he could hear his heartbeat in his chest.
exercises.zh: 寂靜中，他能聽到胸口的心臟跳動。
exercises.upgrade: the heart's beating · 心臟的跳動

options.explanation: quiet, sensory narration makes this descriptive possessive phrase natural.
not heard.
numeric measurement.
not heard.
too technical for the literary/sensory framing.
would be a numerical concept, not the audible phenomenon.

exercises.original: Fear made her heartbeat feel stronger and louder.
exercises.zh: 恐懼令她感到心臟跳動更強、更響。
exercises.upgrade: the heart's beating · 心臟跳動

options.explanation: feel stronger and louder refers to the perceived action of beating, not a measured parameter.
a blood-pressure calculation, not subjective loudness.
volume per minute.
different measure.
technical and not usually described as “louder”.
not English.

exercises.original: The room was so quiet that the heartbeat seemed to fill the silence.
exercises.zh: 房間靜得彷彿心臟的跳動填滿了寂靜。
exercises.upgrade: the heart's beating · 心臟的跳動

options.explanation: the sentence is descriptive and auditory, making this phrase stylistically appropriate.
a number cannot “fill the silence”.
not audible.
not audible.
too technical and abstract.
not standard English.

words.note: 正式詞，表示有節奏的膨脹／收縮或脈動，可描述心臟、血管或其他有規律的搏動。
words.example: The clinician noted a strong pulsation in the artery.
words.exampleZh: 臨床人員注意到動脈有強烈搏動。

exercises.original: The clinician felt a strong heartbeat-like movement in the artery.
exercises.zh: 臨床人員感到動脈有強烈脈動。

options.explanation: artery + strong rhythmic movement is a formal medical use of pulsation.
the artery displays a pulsation caused by rhythm but is not itself the cardiac rhythm.
rate is numeric.
pressure varies with pulsation but is a different concept.
one full heart cycle, not the artery's palpable movement.
adjective, not noun.

exercises.original: A visible heartbeat-like movement could be seen in the vessel.
exercises.zh: 血管中可看到明顯脈動。

options.explanation: visible rhythmic expansion in a vessel is exactly a pulsation.
rhythm is the timing pattern, not the visible physical movement.
numeric.
pressure cannot itself be “seen” in this direct visual sense.
auditory, not visual.
participle/adjective; the sentence requires a noun after a visible.

exercises.original: The scan showed a regular heartbeat-like expansion of the vessel wall.
exercises.zh: 掃描顯示血管壁有規律的脈動性擴張。

options.explanation: regular expansion/contraction of a vessel wall is a pulsation.
may cause expansion but is not the movement itself.
frequency only.
frequency of peripheral pulses, not the wall movement noun.
heart physiology, not vessel-wall motion.
verb form.

words.note: 表示強烈、可感覺到的規律搏動；可形容心跳，也可形容疼痛處的跳痛。
words.example: He could feel the throb of his heart after the sprint.
words.exampleZh: 短跑後，他能感到心臟怦怦跳。

exercises.original: After the sprint, he could feel his heartbeat pounding strongly in his chest.
exercises.zh: 短跑後，他能感到胸口強烈怦怦跳。
exercises.upgrade: throb · 有力的跳動；怦怦跳

options.explanation: pounding strongly is the decisive clue. Throb conveys a strong, perceptible beat.
too technical and not about subjective strength.
not the felt pounding event.
pattern, not forcefulness.
speed/number, not strong sensation.
throbbing can be adjective/participle, but after the ... of the noun throb is more natural.

exercises.original: She felt the heartbeat strongly after climbing the stairs quickly.
exercises.zh: 她快速爬樓梯後感到心臟怦怦跳。

options.explanation: strongly felt beat after exertion is the natural context for throb.
too vague and not the beat sensation.
technical volume measure.
could be elevated, but feeling the heart strongly is about intensity.
technical process.
throbbed is a verb form, not a noun.

exercises.original: In the tense silence, the heartbeat seemed almost painfully strong.
exercises.zh: 緊張的寂靜中，心跳強烈得幾乎令人不適。

options.explanation: painfully strong gives the vivid, forceful-beating nuance associated with throb.
does not express strength.
numeric frequency.
pattern only.
different physiological measure.
rare/awkward adverb and not the noun required.

words.note: 是和 heartbeat 高度相關但更窄的測量概念：每分鐘心跳多少次。
words.example: Her heart rate rose during exercise.

exercises.original: Her heartbeat increased from 70 to 120 beats per minute during exercise.
exercises.zh: 她運動時心率由每分鐘 70 次升至 120 次。
exercises.upgrade: heart rate · 心率；每分鐘心跳次數

options.explanation: beats per minute is the definition of heart rate.
rhythm says regularity/pattern, not bpm value.
one individual event cannot rise from 70 to 120.
physical rhythmic movement, not per-minute measurement.
measured in mmHg, not bpm.
not a physiological term.

exercises.original: The watch displays the user's heartbeat as a number of beats per minute.
exercises.zh: 手錶以每分鐘心跳次數顯示使用者的心率。

options.explanation: numeric bpm display is precisely heart rate.
pattern may require more than a simple bpm number.
one physiological cycle, not a displayed rate.
auditory event.
blood-pressure-derived value.
does not match the numerical definition.

exercises.original: The trainer asked her to keep her heartbeat below 150 beats per minute.
exercises.zh: 教練要求她把心率保持在每分鐘 150 次以下。

options.explanation: a numerical threshold in bpm is a heart-rate target.
regularity, not numeric speed.
one individual event cannot be “below 150 bpm”.
not bpm.
not a frequency target.
a descriptive phrase could explain the concept, but heart rate is the standard noun.

words.note: 指每分鐘可測得的脈搏次數，通常與 heart rate 很接近，但兩者概念上仍有區別。
words.example: The nurse recorded his pulse rate before the procedure.
words.exampleZh: 護士在程序開始前記錄了他的脈率。

exercises.original: The nurse counted his heartbeat at the wrist for sixty seconds.
exercises.zh: 護士在手腕數六十秒脈搏，以取得脈率。
exercises.upgrade: pulse rate · 脈率；每分鐘脈搏次數

options.explanation: wrist + counting for sixty seconds is a direct pulse-rate measurement.
one physiological cycle, not per-minute count.
different technique and unit.
counting for sixty seconds yields rate; rhythm may also be assessed, but it is not the primary noun here.
not measured at the wrist.
not the standard medical term.

exercises.original: Her heartbeat measured at the wrist rose after she stood up.
exercises.zh: 她站起來後，手腕測得的脈率上升。

options.explanation: wrist measurement + rose refers to the frequency of palpable arterial pulses.
would be described as becoming irregular/regular, not usually simply “rose”.
not measured at the wrist.
standing can affect BP, but the sentence explicitly concerns a wrist pulse count.
not a rate measurement.
pulse rate here functions as a noun phrase.

exercises.original: The chart records the patient's heartbeat count taken from the radial pulse.
exercises.zh: 圖表記錄從橈動脈取得的每分鐘脈搏次數。
exercises.upgrade: pulse rate · 每分鐘脈搏次數

options.explanation: radial pulse + count is the exact clinical concept.
pattern, not count.
different vital sign.
volume/min.
one complete beat physiology.
not a standard medical term.

words.meaning: 心臟活動；心電活動／搏動活動
words.note: 較廣的醫療術語，可包括心跳、節律和電活動等，不是 heartbeat 的精確一對一同義詞。
words.example: The monitor detected normal cardiac activity.
words.exampleZh: 監察器偵測到正常的心臟活動。

exercises.original: The monitor detected the baby's heartbeat and other signs that the heart was functioning.
exercises.zh: 監察器偵測到嬰兒的心臟活動，包括心跳及其他心臟功能跡象。
exercises.upgrade: cardiac activity · 心臟活動；心電／搏動活動

options.explanation: heartbeat and other signs that the heart was functioning makes the concept broader than one beat, rate, or rhythm.
far too narrow.
only one measurement.
also narrower and not necessarily directly cardiac.

exercises.original: The device is designed to detect heartbeat-related electrical and mechanical signals.
exercises.zh: 裝置旨在偵測與心臟活動有關的電學和機械訊號。

options.explanation: electrical + mechanical signals explicitly broaden the concept beyond simple heartbeat count.
just frequency.
peripheral frequency.
auditory component only.
vascular pressure, not all cardiac signals.
wrong word class.

exercises.original: The scan confirmed that heartbeat-related activity was present.
exercises.zh: 掃描確認存在心臟活動。

options.explanation: was present asks whether the heart is showing activity at all, so this broader clinical category is natural.
requires measurable frequency.
requires peripheral pulse.
requires a series of beats to analyse pattern.
narrower than presence of activity.
in this physiological sense cardiac activity is normally uncountable.

words.meaning: 心動週期；一次完整心臟循環
words.note: 技術術語，指一次完整心跳中的收縮與舒張循環。它不是單純「一聲心跳」，但在生理學語境可作精確的較窄相關概念。
words.example: Each cardiac cycle includes contraction and relaxation.
words.exampleZh: 每個心動週期都包括收縮與舒張。

exercises.original: The physiology diagram shows what happens during one complete heartbeat, from contraction through relaxation.
exercises.zh: 生理圖表顯示一次完整心跳從收縮到舒張所發生的過程。

options.explanation: from contraction through relaxation is the defining physiological sequence of one cardiac cycle.
counts cycles/beats per minute rather than describing one cycle's phases.
pattern across repeated cycles.
peripheral count.
changes during the cycle but is not the cycle itself.
not the standard physiology term.

exercises.original: Each heartbeat includes a contraction phase followed by a relaxation phase.
exercises.zh: 每個心動週期包括收縮期，之後是舒張期。

options.explanation: the two physiological phases define the full cycle.
frequency, not phase sequence.
same.
timing pattern across cycles.
a variable affected by the cycle.
not the standard term.

exercises.original: The animation slows down a single heartbeat so students can see the filling and pumping phases.
exercises.zh: 動畫把一次完整心跳放慢，讓學生看清充盈與泵血階段。
exercises.upgrade: cardiac cycle · 一次完整心臟循環

options.explanation: single + filling and pumping phases indicates one complete physiological cycle.
a rate cannot be “slowed down” into visible phases in this grammatical sense.
also a frequency.
describes repeated timing pattern rather than one cycle's internal phases.
not the full sequence.
not the standard term for the single-cycle concept.

falseSynonyms.zh: 兩者常同步，因此日常容易混用，但醫療上應分清。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The monitor recorded her heartbeat. The nurse felt her pulse at the wrist.

falseSynonyms.zh: heartbeat 是事件；heart rate 是每分鐘有多少次 heartbeat。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON I could hear each heartbeat. His heart rate was 72 beats per minute.

falseSynonyms.zh: 你可以有正常 heartbeat，但 rhythm 可能規律或不規律；rhythm 不等於單獨一次 beat。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON The device detected every heartbeat. The doctor checked whether the rhythm was regular.

falseSynonyms.zh: 它是測量值，不是跳動聲／跳動事件。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON She felt a strong heartbeat. Her pulse rate increased after exercise.

falseSynonyms.zh: blood pressure 是血液對血管壁的壓力；雖與心臟功能有關，但不是 heartbeat。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON His heartbeat was rapid. His blood pressure was also elevated.

falseSynonyms.zh: 一次 heartbeat 會產生心音，但 heart sound 著重可聽到的聲學現象。
